name: Reels — Build and Verify
description: Cuts the captain's APPROVED reel moments out of an existing master timeline onto their own Resolve timelines, and grades what was built against the plan it was built from. A SECOND product beside edit_video, not a phase of it.

inputs.name: project_folder
inputs.description: Absolute path to the project. It must carry an approved reel plan, a timeline transcript, and a project.yaml naming the Resolve project and its master timeline.

outputs.name: reel_build
outputs.description: What was placed: the timelines built, the plan they came from, and the caption content hashes recorded at build time.

outputs.name: reel_verification
outputs.description: The conformance verdict over what was built. A failure raises; this key existing means the reels conformed.

components.role: Cut every approved moment onto its own timeline
Grade the built timelines against the plan

metadata.author: prajwal
metadata.notes: Why this is a second process rather than nodes of edit_video is measured in docs/REEL_BUILD_HAS_NO_OWNING_NODE.md. It REUSES steps 4.01 and 4.05 through the operation registry (reel_build.reel_subtitle_segments) rather than growing a parallel caption path; library/steps/ is one tree and belongs to the repository, not to a process. There is no runner here: the two nodes are driven through library/tools/operations.py, which is what `manage_project.py build-reels` now does, because two of the five stages that make a reel are outside any DAG by construction - the transcript needs Resolve open and WhisperX loaded, and the approval is the captain's act.
